chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever invests capital and stipulates half the profit, there is no guarantee (of loss) upon him."
And he said: "Whoever provides capital to a merchant, he is entitled only to his principal capital and has no share in the profit."
ai.seo_question: What are the rules of profit and loss in Islamic mudarabah partnership?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Imam al-Baqir from Imam Ali, establishes the foundational principles of mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership) in Shia jurisprudence. It clarifies that if an investor stipulates a fixed profit share without guaranteeing capital loss, they bear no liability for losses; conversely, if they merely provide capital without active management, they are entitled only to their principal, not the profit. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on risk-sharing and the separation of capital provision from managerial effort in commercial contracts.
